Change Control

A formalized process for requesting, evaluating, approving, and tracking infrastructure or configuration changes to minimize risk and ensure auditability.

Questions and answers

Questions and answers

What is Change Control?

In this glossary, Change Control refers to: A formalized process for requesting, evaluating, approving, and tracking infrastructure or configuration changes to minimize risk and ensure auditability.

How is Change Control used in IT and DevOps?

In IT and DevOps communication, this term appears in contexts such as: "All infrastructure updates must go through change control to meet compliance and audit requirements."

Why does Change Control matter in IT and DevOps?

Change Control matters because it supports clear communication in Infrastructure as Code contexts for DevOps Engineers, SREs, and Platform Engineers. It also connects to aviation training and exam language such as AWS Certification, Azure Certification, ITIL v4, and CKA/CKAD.

Who uses Change Control?

Change Control is mainly used by DevOps Engineers, SREs, and Platform Engineers.

What category does Change Control belong to?

In this glossary, Change Control is grouped under Infrastructure as Code. Related pages in this category explain adjacent procedures, commands and operational concepts.

Where does this definition come from?

This definition is sourced from ITIL v4, AWS Well-Architected Framework, Kubernetes Documentation, CNCF and published by Protermify IT/DevOps as a static IT and DevOps reference page.
